title: RAW UNREVIEWED: otor is a portable count expression rather than a star identity
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. GDT1071 fixes one genuine local attachment of exact otor to a six-point, coreless star at f68r1.26; GDT1072 then finds the whole widely in admitted Herbal and other running text, disfavoring an exclusive name for that one star. A count architecture would interpret the star use as a quantified visible feature and the running uses as numeric arguments in complete passages, not infer 'six' merely from six rays. Freeze all 40 source loci and rival full-context readings without selecting convenient Herbal hits. A portable cardinal reading predicts an independently owned counted object and a compatible count-phrase role in nonstellar prose, plus a distinction from nearby measure/unit expressions; a star-name/class reading predicts neither general quantity syntax nor stable counted objects outside the star field. Generic address or property readings remain rivals. Missing input: an independently readable nonstellar count/measure owner and a second physical-folio object-to-word quantity relation. The closed direct-star-ray route must not be rescored with existing f68 labels or proximity matches; this is only a raw architecture for future genuinely new evidence.

design.mechanism: a complete word can name a cardinal quantity applied to different countable referents across picture and prose registers
design.unit: GDT1072 complete admitted otor occurrence set, with f68r1.26 as one source-owned visual occurrence
design.contrast: portable counted quantity versus star identity/class versus nonnumeric property/address
design.prediction: Quantity requires both a nonstellar independently owned counted referent in a complete passage and consistent quantity-argument syntax across all eligible otor uses; star identity/class does not predict that pattern. A single six-ray star is insufficient.
design.missing_input: independent nonstellar count and a second physical-folio singular quantity binding
